FISH 250.title: Marine Biology
FISH 250.description: Lecture-laboratory course in marine biology focusing on physical, biological, and social aspects of the marine environment. Topics include oceanography, ecology, physiology, behavior, conservation, fisheries, exploration, and activism. Weekend field trip. Honors section research project. Course equivalent to: FHL 250 (when FISH 250/BIOL 250/OCEAN 250 is 5 credits). Course overlaps with FHL 250 (when FISH 250/BIOL 250/OCEAN 250 is 3 credits ).

OCEAN 250.title: Marine Biology
OCEAN 250.description: Lecture-laboratory course in marine biology focusing on physical, biological, and social aspects of the marine environment. Topics include oceanography, ecology, physiology, behavior, conservation, fisheries, exploration, and activism. Weekend field trip. Honors section research project. Course equivalent to: FHL 250 (when FISH 250/BIOL 250/OCEAN 250 is 5 credits). Course overlaps with FHL 250 (when FISH 250/BIOL 250/OCEAN 250 is 3 credits ).

BIOL 250.title: Marine Biology
BIOL 250.description: Lecture-laboratory course in marine biology focusing on physical, biological, and social aspects of the marine environment. Topics include oceanography, ecology, physiology, behavior, conservation, fisheries, exploration, and activism. Weekend field trip. Honors section research project. Course equivalent to: FHL 250 (when FISH 250/BIOL 250/OCEAN 250 is 5 credits). Course overlaps with FHL 250 (when FISH 250/BIOL 250/OCEAN 250 is 3 credits ).

CHEM 142.title: General Chemistry I
CHEM 142.description: For science and engineering majors. Atomic nature of matter, quantum mechanics, ionic and covalent bonding, molecular geometry, stoichiometry, solution stoichiometry, and gas laws. Includes laboratory. Maximum 6 credits allowed between CHEM 120; CHEM 142; CHEM 143; CHEM 145; B CHEM 115; B CHEM 143; and B CHEM 144. Course overlaps with: CHEM 120; CHEM 143; CHEM 145; B CHEM 115; B CHEM 143; and T CHEM 142.
CHEM 142.otherPrerequisites: Entry may require CHEM 110, the General Chemistry Placement Exam, or approved AP placement.

CHEM 152.title: General Chemistry II
CHEM 152.description: Gas phase and aqueous equilibria (with emphasis on acid-base equilibrium), thermochemistry, thermodynamics, and electrochemistry. Includes laboratory. Maximum 6 credits allowed between CHEM 152; CHEM 153; CHEM 155; B CHEM 153; and B CHEM 154. Course overlaps with: CHEM 153; CHEM 155; B CHEM 153; and T CHEM 152.

Q SCI 291.title: Calculus for Natural Systems I: Derivatives
Q SCI 291.description: Introduction to differential calculus, emphasizing development of basic skills. Examples promote understanding of mathematics and applications to modeling and solving biological problems. Topics include optimization and curve analysis. Cannot be taken for credit if student received a minimum grade of 2.0 or above in MATH 124 (or equivalent). Course overlaps with: MATH 112; B MATH 144; and TMATH 122.
Q SCI 291.otherPrerequisites: Requires the catalog-listed precalculus preparation or qualifying AP placement.

Q SCI 292.title: Calculus for Natural Systems II: Integrals
Q SCI 292.description: Introduction to integral calculus, emphasizing development of basic skills. Examples promote understanding of mathematics and applications to modeling and solving biological problems. Topics include areas under curves, volumes, and differential equations. Cannot be taken for credit if student received a minimum grade of 2.0 or above in MATH 125 (or equivalent).

MATH 124.title: Calculus with Analytic Geometry I
MATH 124.description: First quarter in calculus of functions of a single variable. Emphasizes differential calculus. Emphasizes applications and problem solving using the tools of calculus. Course equivalent to: STMATH 124 and TMATH 124. Course overlaps with: MATH 112; B MATH 144; STMATH 113; STMATH 114; and TMATH 122. Recommended: completion of Department of Mathematics' Guided Self-Placement.
MATH 124.otherPrerequisites: Requires placement or an accepted prerequisite route.

MATH 125.title: Calculus with Analytic Geometry II
MATH 125.description: Second quarter in the calculus of functions of a single variable. Emphasizes integral calculus. Emphasizes applications and problem solving using the tools of calculus. Cannot be taken for credit if credit has already been earned for MATH 207. Course equivalent to: STMATH 125 and TMATH 125.

BIOL 180.title: Introductory Biology
BIOL 180.description: Mendelian genetics, evolution, biodiversity of life forms, ecology, and conservation biology. Open to all students interested in biology whether intending to major in the biological sciences, enroll in preprofessional programs, or fulfill a Natural World requirement. First course in a three-quarter series (BIOL 180, BIOL 200, BIOL 220). Maximum 15 credits allowed between BIOL 180; BIOL 200; BIOL 220 (or equivalents); and BIOL 240. Course equivalent to: B BIO 180. Course overlaps with: T BIOL 120.

BIOL 200.title: Introductory Biology
BIOL 200.description: For students intending to take advanced courses in the biological sciences or enroll in preprofessional programs. Metabolism and energetics, structure and function of biomolecules, cell structure and function, developmental patterning. Second course in a three-quarter series (BIOL 180, BIOL 200, BIOL 220). Maximum 15 credits allowed between BIOL 180; BIOL 200; BIOL 220 (or equivalents); and BIOL 240. Course equivalent to: B BIO 200. Course overlaps with: T BIOL 130.
BIOL 200.otherPrerequisites: Some approved chemistry choices may be taken concurrently; the sample plan places chemistry earlier.

BIOL 220.title: Introductory Biology
BIOL 220.description: For students intending to take advanced courses in the biological sciences or enroll in preprofessional programs. Animal physiology, plant development and physiology. Final course in a three-quarter series (BIOL 180, BIOL 200, BIOL 220). Maximum 15 credits allowed between BIOL 180; BIOL 200; BIOL 220 (or equivalents); and BIOL 240. Course equivalent to: B BIO 220. Course overlaps with: T BIOL 140.

MARBIO 270.title: Aquatic Ecophysiology
MARBIO 270.description: Focuses on fundamental physiology, with an emphasis on processes relevant to living in a variety of aquatic environments. Includes a broad survey of taxa, from prokaryotes to mammals, and a variety of aquatic habitats.

FISH 270.title: Aquatic Ecophysiology
FISH 270.description: Focuses on fundamental physiology, with an emphasis on processes relevant to living in a variety of aquatic environments. Includes a broad survey of taxa, from prokaryotes to mammals, and a variety of aquatic habitats.

OCEAN 270.title: Aquatic Ecophysiology
OCEAN 270.description: Focuses on fundamental physiology, with an emphasis on processes relevant to living in a variety of aquatic environments. Includes a broad survey of taxa, from prokaryotes to mammals, and a variety of aquatic habitats.

Q SCI 381.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics
Q SCI 381.description: Applications to biological and natural resource problems stressing the formulation and interpretation of statistical tests. Random variables, expectations, variances, binomial, hypergeometric, Poisson, normal, chi-square, "t" and "F" distributions. Course overlaps with: STMATH 341; STMATH 390; and TME 351.

STAT 311.title: Elements of Statistical Methods
STAT 311.description: Elements of good study design. Descriptive statistics including correlation and regression. Introductory concepts of probability and sampling; binomial and normal distributions. Basic concepts of hypothesis testing, estimation, and confidence intervals; t-tests and chi-square tests. Experience with computer software. Course overlaps with: STMATH 341.

PHYS 114.title: Mechanics
PHYS 114.description: Principles of mechanics using algebra-based modeling with an emphasis on applications in life sciences. Maximum 5 credits allowed between PHYS 114; PHYS 117; PHYS 121; and PHYS 141 (or equivalents). Course equivalent to: B PHYS 114. Course overlaps with: PHYS 121; PHYS 141; and B PHYS 121.

PHYS 115.title: Heat, Fluids and Electricity and Magnetism
PHYS 115.description: Principles of heat, fluids, and electromagnetism using algebra-based modeling with an emphasis on applications in life sciences. Maximum 5 credits allowed between PHYS 115; PHYS 118; PHYS 122; and PHYS 142 (or equivalents). Course equivalent to: B PHYS 115. Course overlaps with: PHYS 122; PHYS 142; and B PHYS 122.

PHYS 121.title: Mechanics
PHYS 121.description: Basic principles of mechanics and experiments in mechanics for physical science and engineering majors. Lecture tutorial and lab components must all be taken to receive credit. Maximum 5 credits allowed between PHYS 114; PHYS 117; PHYS 121; and PHYS 141 (or equivalents). Course equivalent to: B PHYS 121. Course overlaps with: PHYS 114; PHYS 117; PHYS 141; B PHYS 114; and B PHYS 117.
PHYS 121.otherPrerequisites: Requires MATH 124 or MATH 134, which may be taken concurrently, or approved placement.

PHYS 122.title: Electromagnetism
PHYS 122.description: overs the basic principles of electromagnetism and experiments in these topics for physical science and engineering majors. Lecture tutorial and lab components must all be taken to receive credit. Maximum 5 credits allowed between PHYS 115; PHYS 118; PHYS 122; and PHYS 142 (or equivalents). Course equivalent to: B PHYS 122. Course overlaps with: PHYS 115; PHYS 118; PHYS 142; B PHYS 115; and B PHYS 118.

OCEAN 285.title: Physics Across Oceanography: Fluid Mechanics and Waves
OCEAN 285.description: In the context of oceanography applications, explores fluid mechanics, waves, light, acoustics, and heat transfer.

OCEAN 286.title: Physics Across Oceanography: Fluid Mechanics and Waves Laboratory
OCEAN 286.description: Laboratory and tutorial further exploring the oceanography applications of fluid mechanics, waves, light, acoustics, and heat transfer.

OCEAN 200.title: Introduction to Oceanography
OCEAN 200.description: Focuses on importance of ocean processes for the functioning of our planet. Interdisciplinary case studies are used to examine relationships and interactions at macro-, meso-, and microscales in the ocean. Case studies build upon previous topics and examines human influence on these systems. Intended for science majors.

OCEAN 201.title: Introduction to Oceanography Lab
OCEAN 201.description: Provides opportunities to experiment with oceanographic concepts through laboratory and field experiences. Students apply the scientific method of inquiry as it applies to the study of geology, physics, chemistry, and biology of the ocean. Emphasizes topics that explore current challenges faced by the ocean and its ecosystem. Co-requisite: OCEAN 200.

OCEAN 210.title: Integrative Oceans
OCEAN 210.description: Presents fundamentals of ocean science through regional case studies that illustrate the relationship between interdependent physical, chemical, biological, and geological process. Students apply tools from these scientific disciplines to understand major changes predicted for future oceanic environments.

MARBIO 305.title: Scientific Writing in Marine Biology
MARBIO 305.description: Introduces the fundamentals of scientific writing about research in marine biology: content, organization, critical thinking, structure, and the mechanics of grammar, wording, and formatting. Students critically evaluate scientific writing in this discipline, and practice developing, writing, and revising concise arguments supported by scientific evidence. Course overlaps with: FHL 333.
MARBIO 305.otherPrerequisites: Requires one course that satisfies the UW English Composition requirement.

FHL 333.title: Science Writing for Diverse Audiences
FHL 333.description: Examines the effective communication of scientific ideas in writing for both scientific and public audiences. Students read, analyze, and write diverse materials, learning to identify and practice concise, effective communication about marine science for a variety of audiences. The close-knit, hands-on FHL community creates an environment where students work together both inside and outside of class to build their skills. Course overlaps with: MARBIO 305.
FHL 333.otherPrerequisites: Approved communication alternative, but the department states that it is currently not offered.

OCEAN 295.title: Chemistry of Marine Organic Carbon
OCEAN 295.description: Explores the movement of organic carbon through the global carbon cycle, in the context of earth sciences and marine biogeochemical cycles.

FISH 323.title: Conservation and Management of Aquatic Resources
FISH 323.description: Topics include population dynamics, extinction risk, meta-populations, marine reserves, bioeconomics, protection of endangered species, sustainable harvesting, and management institutions. Examines case studies such as salmon, albatross, and whales as representative of conservation issues in aquatic sciences. Sampling, experimental design, computer skills, and research writing.

MARBIO 370.title: Marine Evolutionary Biology
MARBIO 370.description: Emphasizes geobiological patterns of marine evolutionary biology environment; processes of evolution; marine prokaryote and eukaryote diversity; and applications of evolutionary principles to ocean change, and conservation and management of marine biodiversity.

FISH 370.title: Marine Evolutionary Biology
FISH 370.description: Emphasizes geobiological patterns of marine evolutionary biology environment; processes of evolution; marine prokaryote and eukaryote diversity; and applications of evolutionary principles to ocean change, and conservation and management of marine biodiversity.

OCEAN 370.title: Marine Evolutionary Biology
OCEAN 370.description: Emphasizes geobiological patterns of marine evolutionary biology environment; processes of evolution; marine prokaryote and eukaryote diversity; and applications of evolutionary principles to ocean change, and conservation and management of marine biodiversity.

OCEAN 330.title: Marine Biogeochemical Cycles
OCEAN 330.description: overs the distribution of life and chemical elements in the ocean; the relationship between them; and the physical processes affecting these patterns. Emphasizes how marine organisms and the structure of marine ecosystems influence the fate of carbon and other elements in the ocean.

MARBIO 488.title: Marine Biology in the Field
MARBIO 488.description: Uses extensive field work to enhance students' practical knowledge of marine organismal and habitat diversity, and oceanographic processes. Develops integrative skills in experimental design, data collection, field interpretation, and communication.

FHL 403.title: Novel Marine Ecosystems
FHL 403.description: overs how novel marine ecosystems arise from extinctions, introductions, climate change, and habitat change. Students apply fundamental ecological concepts to investigate novel ecosystem dynamics and management. Uses place-based, field-based, and project-based learning. Teaches hands-on scientific and professional skills in ecological theory and practice.

FHL 420.title: Marine Ecology of the Salish Sea
FHL 420.description: Field-oriented study of ecology of the Salish Sea. Students live and study at the Friday Harbor Laboratories, a seaside setting for immersive learning. Students observe relationships between coastal organisms and their environment, and explore processes by which these relationships change over time and location. Lecture, field, and laboratory activities focus on habitats and species of ecological, economic, and/or cultural importance.

FHL 467.title: Behavioral Ecology of Marine Invertebrates
FHL 467.description: overs ecological behaviors of marine invertebrates linking organismal, ecological, and evolutionary biology. Focuses on the development of integrative field and lab skills spanning observation, hypotheses, study design, data collection, analysis, and communication.

FHL 470.title: Research in Marine Biology
FHL 470.description: A hands-on introduction of "doing science" in close collaboration with a faculty member. Students engage in research in marine biology, which may include lab experiments and field work. Students gather, analyze, write up, and present their own data.
FHL 470.otherPrerequisites: When used for the Integrative Field Experience, 6 credits apply to that requirement; do not also count the same credits toward electives.

FHL 450.title: Nearshore Ecology Research Experience
FHL 450.description: A hands-on introduction of "doing science" in close collaboration with a faculty member. Students engage in research around a thematic focus of ecology of nearshore marine ecosystems, with lab experiments and field work. Students gather, analyze, write up, and present their own data.
FHL 450.otherPrerequisites: May satisfy the Integrative Field Experience when approved; do not double-count the same credits as electives.

FHL 432.title: Marine Invertebrate Zoology
FHL 432.description: omparative morphology and biology of marine invertebrates with emphasis on field and laboratory studies. Representatives of all major and most minor phyla are collected, observed live, and studied in detail. Taken at Friday Harbor Laboratories. Cannot be taken if credit received for BIOL 434. Course overlaps with: FISH 310.

FHL 468.title: Advanced Topics in Ecology and Biomechanics
FHL 468.description: Focuses on various aspects of ecology and biomechanics of marine organisms, such as experimental ecology, ocean acidification, deep sea biodiversity, or biomechanics. Taught at Friday Harbor Laboratories.
FHL 468.otherPrerequisites: Only department-approved sections count; IFE approval varies by offering.

FHL 492.title: Ecology and Conservation of Marine Birds and Mammals
FHL 492.description: An intensive, field-based course that offers motivated students the opportunity to learn about these ecologically and culturally important marine animals and the conservation problems they face. Emphasizes first-hand learning and individual research projects.

FHL 472.title: Friday Harbor Labs Research Apprenticeship
FHL 472.description: A full-time, quarter-long program where apprentices work intensively on learning methods and carrying out hands-on research around one theme. Themes vary with the quarter and involve either extensive field or laboratory work or both. Students are trained in context, tools, data-gathering, and creation of research products appropriate to the theme. Recommended: strong background in core biological sciences.
FHL 472.otherPrerequisites: Only approved apprenticeship sections count toward the Integrative Field Experience.

mapGroups.label: Declaration & General Education
mapGroups.description: Marine Biology may be declared while in good academic standing. Complete College of the Environment general education requirements.

mapGroups.label: Biology, Calculus & Statistics
mapGroups.description: Introductory biology, two quarters of calculus, and one statistics course.

mapGroups.label: Physics
mapGroups.description: Choose algebra-based, calculus-based, or the approved oceanography-physics route.

mapGroups.label: Introduction to the Marine Environment
mapGroups.description: Introductory marine science, Integrative Oceans, and scientific communication.

mapGroups.label: Marine Biology Core
mapGroups.description: Conservation and management, marine evolutionary biology, and marine biogeochemical cycles.

mapGroups.label: Electives — Biodiversity
mapGroups.description: One approved biodiversity course; eligible courses may also satisfy laboratory and 400-level subrequirements.

mapGroups.label: Electives — Ecology & Ecosystems
mapGroups.description: One approved ecology and ecosystems course.

mapGroups.label: Other Approved Marine Biology Electives
mapGroups.description: Additional approved electives, research, and approved special topics. The full elective program also requires two labs and three 400-level courses.

mapGroups.label: Integrative Field Experience
mapGroups.description: Culminating field experience away from the Seattle campus; most options require a Friday Harbor Labs application.

mapGroups.label: Additional Degree Requirements
mapGroups.description: Major GPA, UW residency, outside-major Natural Science, and total-credit checks.

requirements.note: Marine Biology is an open major. Students may declare after enrolling at UW while in good academic standing; there are no course prerequisites for declaration.

requirements.title: Independent Research and Internship Limit
requirements.note: Confirm that no more than 6 credits total of independent research or internship are applied to the 25-credit elective requirement.

requirements.title: Integrative Field Experience
requirements.note: Starting Autumn 2026, eligible 5-credit courses satisfy the IFE. Other approved options carry 6, 9, or 15 credits. Most options require a Friday Harbor Labs application, and section-specific approval may apply.

requirements.title: IFE and Elective Credit Allocation
requirements.note: Confirm that credits used for the Integrative Field Experience are not also counted toward Marine Biology electives when the department marks the course as either/or.

requirements.title: Minimum GPA in Courses Presented for the Major
requirements.note: Enter 1 or mark fulfilled after confirming a minimum 2.00 cumulative GPA in courses presented for the major.

requirements.title: UW Residency Requirement
requirements.note: Confirm at least 45 credits as a matriculated UW student and at least 45 of the final 60 credits taken at UW.

requirements.title: Total Degree Credits
requirements.note: Includes general education, foundation science and mathematics, Marine Biology requirements, and general electives.

samplePlan.name: Official UW Marine Biology four-year plan (one coherent course-choice path; editable)
samplePlan.note: The department's official four-year plan uses alternative course labels. This version selects CHEM 142/152 plus OCEAN 295, Q SCI 291/292, MARBIO 270, PHYS 114/115, and FISH 250 to avoid duplicate alternatives. Course availability varies by quarter and year.

Natural Sciences Outside Major.note: Choose an NSc course outside Marine Biology major prefixes that is not also applied to major requirements.
